  • dtcg — W3C DTCG JSON. Canonical pivot format. Round-trip safe via `$extensions["figma-console-mcp"]`.
  • css-vars — CSS custom properties with mode-aware selectors (`:root`, `.dark`, `[data-theme=...]`).

collectionIds.description: Specific Figma collection IDs to export. Required when scope is 'collection'. Use figma_get_variables to enumerate available collections.

tools.name: rigour_check
tools.description: Run quality gate checks on the project. MUST be called before declaring any coding task complete. By default it judges your change as the stop hook and push gate will: FAIL means something in it must be fixed. **Always show the user the headline summary from this tool's output** — it tells them what Rigour caught. If FAIL, call rigour_get_fix_packet for what to fix, with exact file:line.

cwd.description: Absolute path to the project root.

scope.description: 'change' (default): your change, as the stop hook judges it. 'repo': the whole repository, for an audit, not a fix loop.

files.description: Optional file paths (relative to cwd) to limit scan scope for both deterministic and deep checks.

deep.description: Deep mode: 'off' (default), 'quick' (deep enabled with lite model), 'full' (deep enabled, combine with pro=true for full deep model).

pro.description: Use full deep model (Qwen2.5-Coder-1.5B) instead of lite (Qwen2.5-Coder-0.5B) when deep is enabled.

apiKey.description: Optional cloud API key for deep analysis.

provider.description: Cloud provider for deep analysis (claude, openai, gemini, groq, mistral, together, deepseek, ollama, etc.).

apiBaseUrl.description: Custom API base URL for self-hosted/proxy deep endpoints.

modelName.description: Override cloud model name for deep analysis.

tools.name: rigour_get_fix_packet
tools.description: After rigour_check FAILs: your change's must-fix items (they block you), then optional notes, paged, each with file:line and the fix. Stay in your change unless a must-fix item names a file. Page with next_offset; re-run rigour_check.

cwd.description: Absolute path to the project root.

offset.description: Zero-based violation offset. Start at 0, then use the next offset in the response.

tools.name: rigour_remember
tools.description: Store an instruction or convention to remember across sessions. Provide 'key' (short snake_case) and 'value' (the full text). scope: 'repo' (default, this repository), 'user' (all your repositories), or 'team' (this repository, and shared as a team candidate that teammates' agents receive once a person promotes it). Values containing credentials are refused.

cwd.description: Absolute path to the project root.

key.description: A short snake_case identifier for this memory, e.g. 'api_response_format', 'naming_convention', 'testing_strategy'. This is used to retrieve the memory later.

value.description: The full instruction or convention text to persist. This is the content that will be recalled in future sessions.

scope.description: Where the memory applies. Default: repo.

tools.name: rigour_brief
tools.description: Before writing: with goal, the team's rules, lessons and settled points for the task (max 10, cited); with only files, its word on each file you will edit. A [must] you break blocks at review.

cwd.description: Absolute path to the project root.

goal.description: What the task is for: the request or the ticket summary.

files.description: Optional. Files the task will touch.

tools.name: rigour_recall
tools.description: Load stored conventions. At the START of a task, call it with 'query' describing the task to get the few memories that match by meaning, plus promoted team knowledge when team mode is on. With 'key' it returns that memory; with neither, every repository and user memory.

cwd.description: Absolute path to the project root.

key.description: Optional. Key of specific memory to retrieve.

query.description: Optional. What you are about to do, e.g. 'add retry to the payments client'. Returns the closest memories by meaning.

tools.name: rigour_check_pattern
tools.description: CALL THIS BEFORE creating any new function, component, hook, or class. Checks if it already exists in the codebase (prevents duplication), checks for known security vulnerabilities, and BLOCKS writes to protected paths (.github/, CI/CD configs, rigour.yml). Always pass the target file path.

cwd.description: Absolute path to the project root.

name.description: The name of the function, class, or component you want to create.

intent.description: What the code is for (e.g., 'format dates', 'user authentication').

signature.description: Optional. The signature you plan to write, e.g. '(items: T[], size: number) => T[][]'. Matches existing code by shape, not only by name.

keywords.description: Optional. Words for what it does, e.g. ['retry', 'backoff'].

file.description: Target file path (relative to cwd) where the code will be written. Used to enforce protected path rules — writes to .github/, rigour.yml, etc. will be BLOCKED.

tools.name: rigour_review
tools.description: Review the change you just made before calling it done: runs Rigour's gates and keeps only findings on changed lines, each with file, line and a suggested fix. With no diff it reads your uncommitted work from git (new files included); pass base to review the whole branch (e.g. 'main'). Same verdict as `rigour review` in CI.

cwd.description: Absolute path to the project root.

base.description: Review this branch against a base ref instead of uncommitted work, e.g. 'main'.

diff.description: A unified diff to review instead of reading git. Rarely needed.

files.description: Review exactly these files instead of the ones the change touches.

mode.description: "agent": also return review_task, the risky changed functions for you to review yourself, with what to check in each. No model is called by Rigour.

tools.name: rigour_reviewer_verdict
tools.description: What the model reviewer last decided for this branch: the confirmed items to fix (with id, file:line, consequence and evidence), the disputed ones that are not work, which mode ran, and whether the verdict is for the current commit. Read-only: never runs a model, never dismisses.

cwd.description: Absolute path to the project root.

tools.name: rigour_review_ack
tools.description: Record that you reviewed a function from rigour_review's review_task: verdict "fixed" (you fixed a defect) or "no_issue", with a note saying what you checked. Covers the function's current code only; editing it later puts it back in the task.

cwd.description: Absolute path to the project root.

note.description: What you checked, e.g. 'callers pass a non-empty cursor; upsert conflict key matches the unique index'.

tools.name: rigour_index
tools.description: Build or update the Rigour pattern index (.rigour/patterns.json). CALL THIS when the index is missing or stale — before rigour_context_scope or rigour_check_pattern. One AST pass extracts functions, classes, routes, and signatures for reuse, embedded locally so rigour_check_pattern can match by intent; semantic=false skips the embeddings.

cwd.description: Absolute path to the project root.

semantic.description: Embed patterns so an intent can find them (local Transformers.js model). Default: true; false records an explicit opt-out.

force.description: Force a full rebuild instead of incremental update. Default: false.

output.description: Custom path for the index file.

tools.name: rigour_context_scope
tools.description: CALL THIS BEFORE reading source files. Returns a minimal editScope (3-10 files) with signatures from the pattern index instead of full file bodies. Uses semantic search when embeddings are available. If index is missing, instructs to call rigour_index first. Highest-impact token saver in the Rigour protocol.

cwd.description: Absolute path to the project root.

query.description: Natural-language description of what you need to work on (e.g. 'add priority field to task service').

limit.description: Maximum number of pattern matches to return (default: 10).

taskId.description: Optional task ID for context telemetry attribution.

agentId.description: Optional agent ID for context telemetry attribution.
